raw.name: FAQ
raw.content: What is Gray Zone Warfare? Gray Zone Warfare is an immersive tactical PvEvP first-person shooter with a maximum focus on realism. Become a part of a Private Military Company and navigate an expansive open-world setting alone or in a squad. Adapt to your surroundings, use tactics to your advantage, and fight for survival against other human operators and AI-controlled enemies. Who is the developer and publisher? We at Madfinger Games are both the developer and publisher. Are there time limits for each session? We are taking a different approach - there are no time limits for any session. We are aiming to make our gamer more approachable, so you can stay in one session as long as you want. On top of facing the other factions and AI, you will be able to go through the story mode by completing various tasks from vendors. We don’t want anyone to feel forced with limited-time sessions, so you can explore the open-word jungle with your teammates and take your time. If you decide to jump into another session, you will keep the gear that you have and your story progress. What engine are you developing your new game on? We are using the latest Unreal Engine 5. GZW harnesses cutting-edge tech, including the groundbreaking features of Nanite, Lumen, and virtual textures. This enables unprecedented levels of graphical fidelity and realism. What will be the minimum PC configuration requirements for the new game? Our minimum requirement graphical processor chip is RTX 2070. We strive towards the highest visual fidelity. Currently, we are exploring optimization options for the future. How many people are involved in the development of the new game? There are around 80 employees including contractors and remote employees. What platforms will your new game be playable on? We are starting on PC first. Our goal is to make this game as smooth and polished as possible, so we want to start there and see where our path takes us. Will the game be released globally? We would love to share our game with as many people as possible, but some of the themes we touch do not allow this. We will do our best to give the opportunity to play our game to the widest audience possible. How many languages will the game be playable in? Only English for EA. Later on, we will add support for other languages. (Spanish, French, etc) Approximately when do you want to release the game? We'd like to start Early Access in the 1st quarter of 2024. Subject to change, but that is our goal. Will the game be Free-To-Play? Microtransactions? Gray Zone Warfare will be a premium game with no microtransactions.

raw.name: Game modes
raw.content: This page is still heavily in work in progress . Some informations might be incomplete or unconfirmed. Gray Zone Warfare offers three different game modes options for the players. The Warfare game mode allows players from different factions to fight each other anywhere on the map. This is a complete PvPvE game mode. You can be shot at by a player everywhere on the map, even in the base. No safe-zones are present on the map that protects a player from being damaged. The players only gets "invincible" for a few seconds(3-5s) after getting out of a Helicopter on a LZ . In Warfare mode, COPs can be attacked by players when the COP doesn't belong to their faction. In the Warfare mode, COPs are always defended by AI, even when a COP belong to another faction. Those are red circled zones that appear on the map when players from different faction engage a fight nearby. The zone is created upon several actions between players and last for 5 mins after the last shot by one of the players. Here are the conditions for the circle to appears: When faction A player suppress faction B player. When faction A player damage faction B Player. When faction A player kills faction B player. You can hover the zone to get more information about it The zones are also created when players attacks another faction owned COP . The circle is created under those rules: When faction A player suppress faction B AI. When faction A player damage faction B AI. When faction A player kills faction B AI. When faction B AI shoot at faction A player. The circles appears on the map in-between the involved fighters exactly at the center of both players. If multiple players are involved (faction C player is involved for example), multiple circles will appear following the same rule. When a player kills, loot, suppress or damage another player from the same faction , the player gets the Aggressor status. This status is given to the player with a timer, this timer can't exceed 1 hour and is dependent of IRL time, which means that the player will have to wait 1 real hour for it go away. The timer continue to go down if the player is offline, or switch to the Joint Operations (PvE) game mode. There is several downside to having the aggressor status : The player can't loot his own body if he dies. The player can be looted by other player of the same faction "freely" (without getting the aggressor status) if he dies. The player wont be able to report another player. Each negative action against friendly members adds a specific amount of time to the aggressor status timer. Aggressor penalties Type Amount of time Suppression 5 mins Wound damage 10 mins Looting body 30 mins Kill 1 hour PvP Game mode + explanations of how the mode works PvE game mode + explanations of how the mode works They are reserved to community GMs to be uses. Any player can join them as long as they have the invitation code, generated by the GMs. They are often used for communities events hosted by those GMs. They're up for as long as a player stay in the server, they time out after about an hour of being empty or if a GM shut them off. Both game mode progressions are shared, which means that progressing on Joint Operations also progress your character on Warfare mode.

raw.name: Health system
raw.content: The Health system in Gray Zone Warfare doesn't rely on traditional hit points. Instead, it employs a detailed simulation of various body parts and vital pools like blood and hydration. When your character experiences health issues, they're signaled by distinct symptoms, each indicating a specific problem. In Gray Zone Warfare, victory lies not in treating symptoms, but in tackling their root causes head-on. Wounds (red marker): Result from projectile or melee weapon hits that bypass protective gear. Categorized as Light, Medium, or Severe based on bleeding severity. Light wounds heal over time, while others require treatment. Bruises (purple marker): Occur when projectiles are stopped by protective gear, causing pain. They heal naturally after a while. Treated wounds (green marker): Follow treatment of Medium or Severe wounds, causing temporary discomfort before healing. Damaged/Organ damage: Key organs like the brain, heart, lungs, and liver can sustain damage, visible as color changes on X-rays. Destruction of vital organs like the heart or brain results in immediate death. Damaged bones: Arm and leg bones can be damaged by impacts or falls, displayed similarly to organ damage. Blood loss: Losing blood leads to negative symptoms, with severe loss resulting in coma. Blood naturally regenerates unless hydration and energy are critically low. Intoxication: Increases with stimulant use, gradually decreasing or requiring treatment. Radiation: Accumulates in irradiated areas, necessitating treatment to prevent lethal levels. Coma: Players have a limited time to save a comatose character by addressing the underlying causes—usually blood loss or organ damage. Nausea: Stems from various factors like liver injury, radiation exposure, or intoxication. Given the likelihood of liver injury, utilizing a surgery kit becomes imperative to address the issue effectively. You can find a list of all available medical items and what they do here . This page lists every medical item in the game, and their weakness/buffs. Bandages : Treats wounds but not bruises. Tourniquets : Stops bleeding but won't treat wounds. Splints : Repair damaged bones. Surgery Kits : Restore damaged or destroyed organs. Blood Bags : Replenish lost blood. Pain Killers : Pills that can treat pain; details provided in item descriptions. Intoxication Pills : Pills that can cure radiation and intoxication; details provided in item descriptions. Stimulants : Alter Health System behavior with benefits and drawbacks; details provided in item descriptions. The below information is being actively documented through in-game testing and observation. It is heavily subject to change and potential inaccuracy/incompletion due to new game patches and/or insufficient test scenarios. Please be patient as we gather the necessary data. Leg and arm staminas are divided into two separate systems in Gray Zone Warfare. Both share similar traits such as draining or being limited under certain activities or status effects, and otherwise regenerating naturally over time. Each stamina is typically required for its respective activities, and these activities can be rendered impossible if the relevant stamina is fully depleted. Any injuries sustained to the legs or arms will result in a debuff to the appropriate stamina that lowers its maximum recharge capacity until the injury has been dealt with. I.e. The more injured a limb is, the less stamina you will have for it. Leg stamina is used for activities such as sprinting, jumping, vaulting/climbing and wading through water. When leg stamina is fully depleted, all of these activities are temporarily prevented, with the exception of wading through water, which instead incurs a speed penalty. When leg stamina is critically low, the player character will start lurching with heavy breathing. Additionally, the rate of leg stamina drain is seemingly influenced by the player's carry weight, with higher kgs resulting in faster stamina drainage. Arm stamina is used for activities such as aiming/firing a weapon, melee attacks and vaulting/climbing. However, unlike with leg stamina, when arm stamina is fully depleted none of these actions are prevented. Instead, aiming incurs a stability penalty (see below status effects for more info). Additionally, the rate of arm stamina drain whilst aiming is seemingly influenced by the relevant statistic and weight of the equipped weapon, with higher kgs/arm stamina drain stats resulting in faster stamina drainage. There are currently 3 active HUD meters that are only visible outside of the tactical device menu. I.e. When in the primary first-person view of the player character. These meters appear in the top-left corner of the HUD and represent: Arm stamina (left meter) - The percentage of arm stamina available/used. Stance (middle meter) - The current stance that is being assumed, between stand, crouch and prone. Leg stamina (right meter) - The percentage of leg stamina available/used. There is a fourth hidden meter that represents the player's breath/lung capacity. Not a lot is known about how this meter works, other than that it apparently drains whilst breath is held, when lungs are damaged or through sprinting, jumping etc. in a similar manner to leg stamina. When this meter is fully depleted, breath cannot be held and other status effects are applied (see below). Understanding your health status and utilizing appropriate treatments are vital for survival. Stay vigilant by monitoring your Health Panel in the menu for real-time updates on your condition. raw.name: Lamang Island
raw.content: Official country name: The Democratic Republic of Lamang Location: Somewhere in Southeast Asia Area: 430km² Population: 74,470 President: Narith Sayavong Official languages: Lao and English Area of operations: 42km² A former British colony, Lamang was ravaged by a brutal civil war just two decades after gaining its independence when the remnants of the anti-British resistance (known as SOL - Sons of Lamang) were dissatisfied with the independent government‘s rule. Since the official army was understaffed, untrained, and equipped with outdated weapons and gear, it was swiftly defeated after only a couple of months of fighting. The SOL commander, Raksmei Sayavong, then declared himself the supreme leader of the island with the title of President. Raksmei‘s victory was made possible thanks to the help of the Soviets, who supplied the SOL with weapons in exchange for strengthening their position during the Vietnam War. Building various military installations all over Lamang, a small contingent of Soviet troops remained on the island even after the end of the conflict and finally left after the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991. Raksmei Sayavong died in 1996, with his only son, the 28-year-old Narith Sayavong, becoming the new leader of the island. Narith promised the people of Lamang that he would end his late father‘s isolationism policies and bring the island into the next millennium through modernization and openness. Claiming to focus on tourism, he ordered the construction of his crowning jewel - the Midnight Sapphire - a luxurious resort where, legend has it, all was allowed for the right price. During the next three decades, those few who managed to escape the island told a vastly different story and pleaded with the rest of the world for help until, finally, the UN decided to act and established the UNLRA (United Nations Lamang Relief Agency) to provide at least a modicum of assistance to the oppressed people. With Narith‘s hesitant approval, UNLRA arrived in Lamang to assess the situation and begin its humanitarian mission. Then, a few months later, a disaster struck. With a blinding flash and thunderous roar, a part of the island was forever transformed by a sudden cataclysmic Event. The official channels cryptically speak of an unspecified environmental disaster while a plethora of far-fetched theories and “uncovered truths” scour the World Wide Web and beyond. A volcano erupting, a chemical factory exploding, a nuke going off, a satellite crashing, secret experiments gone terribly wrong, a meteorite impact, or the always-popular aliens. It will be up to the players to find out for themselves. What is certain is that all hell broke loose in Lamang after the event. Mass hysteria and panic ensued, and UNLRA mounted an evacuation mission to get as many people off the island as possible. All UNLRA personnel and a majority of the survivors left the island, and the entire area has been put under international quarantine, with all the UN members agreeing not to trespass. Seeing that the island was practically abandoned, many organized crime groups, pirates, and other lowlifes gathered in Lamang to plunder what was left or even claim the island entirely, engaging in skirmishes with the Lamang Armed Forces , who were ordered to stay behind and guard high-value targets. The first PMC , hired by their powerful clients to explore the area, arrived shortly after, followed soon by two others. After establishing a foothold in the region, they all started advancing towards what was now known as Ground Zero. A series of well-coordinated strikes, far too professional for the bandits roaming the island or even Lamang Armed Forces, was then launched against the PMCs, and they lost almost all their previously taken territory. Suffering heavy casualties and loss of equipment, the PMCs started recruiting new soldiers of fortune to help them retake the region, assume full control of Ground Zero, and complete any tasks from the myriad of clients with some stakes in the area. The player, a former member of Special Operation Forces, is one of these new recruits. Lamang is based on the real life southeast Asian country Laos

raw.name: Locations
raw.content: If the problems have been addressed, please edit this page and remove this notice. It will start with {{MissInfos and end with }} . The map of Gray Zone Warfare is an Island that consists of multiple Points of Interest that the player can visit. While the map is still growing with each update, the entire island can be visited freely, by foot, or by using Landing Zones. Lamang Island points of interest are divided into multiple regions. Each region hold a Major point of interest populated by a large amount of enemies, with minor point of interests populating its outskirts populated by a smaller amount of enemies. The player may visit each major POI of each region by completing Tasks Radiation plays a critical role as an environmental hazard that forces players to strategize carefully. Areas contaminated with radiation cause continuous damage to characters who linger too long, making these zones risky to traverse without proper gear or planning. Players will need to use Potassium Iodide to curb the effects of Radiation. Some points of interests features doors that are locked by a key / code / padlock. The codes can be usually found in the same POI in a document / small note / post-it that can be read using your interaction key giving you either information on where to find the code, or the code itself. Mines are placed around the Main Operating Bases of each faction and major COPs, to prevent other factions from attacking the base by any other way other than the main entrance. They are automatically triggered once a player steps on them. There are 3 different operating bases on the island, one for each faction. This is the most important place for every operator as it serves as your main hub. You can prepare your gear, manage your stash, access vendor inventories, respawn, and call a helicopter to get to any LZ's that you have discovered. Major Points of Interest Image Name Description Grid Position Kiu Vongsa The starter town of the faction Crimson Shield International . 141:164 Nam Thaven The starter town of the faction Mithras Security Systems . 171:118 Pha Lang The starter town of the faction Lamang Recovery Initiative . 202:162 Sawmill A tier 2 zone featuring an old sawmill. 139:144 Hunter's Paradise A private shooting range. 159:168 Ban Pa A small town close to water on the east side of the island. 205:137 Pha Lang Airfield The civilian airfield. 182:158 YBL-1 A military underground bunker. 143:122 Blue Lagoon A small resort in the south of the island near the moutains. 203:117 Midnight Sapphire A luxury residential estate in the north of the island. A Hotel in the middle of it. Guarded by the LAF. 171:166 Fort Narith The biggest military site on the Island. The second biggest airfield on the island. 143:129 Tiger Bay The biggest city on the island. A huge commercial center in the middle of it. Now controlled by the LAF. 198:130 Ever since the 0.4 Spearhead update , the Island is now divided into 12 regions centered around the Major POIs. The Faction starter town regions are only visible to their respective factions. Minor points of interest are locations that players can visit. They remain hidden on the map until they have been visited. There are many different types of minor POIs: landing zones military facilities : bases, checkpoints, convoys civil infrastructure: public buildings, houses, stores, garages, motels, farms, shelters, shacks, campsites landscapes: lakes, ponds, viewpoints These locations are the primary places where loot and intel can be found. However, some POIs may be empty. You can find a list of all minor POIs in a region on the page for that region: Ground Zero Kiu Vongsa - only for players from CSI faction. Nam Thaven - only for players from MSS faction. Pha Lang - only for players from LRI faction. In each region, visiting minor POIs helps advance your progress in the Exploration tab. Combat Outposts (COPs) serve as pivotal points for strategic control, offering players opportunities for respawning, restocking, and engaging in both PvP and PvE activities. COPs must first be captured by anyone in your faction before they can be accessed. Their significance is amplified by the dynamic environment and the potential access to Vulture's black market . Captured COPs can be used as respawn points instead of the base camps (base camp respawn is still available anywhere) Players can access their lockers and vendors in the COPs In PvP (Warfare) mode, factions fight for control over COPs. Once a COP is captured, guards spawn to defend it, and rival factions must engage in combat to take control. These outposts become focal points for intense battles, influencing the strategic dynamics of the game. In PvE (Joint Operations) mode, the first faction to capture a COP must fight AI defenders. Once secured, the AI defenders will not spawn again and all other factions can capture it simultaneously and access it freely, turning it into a shared safe zone. This system encourages cooperation among players while still maintaining the challenge of AI opposition. Netural COPs, signified by the gray marker on the Map means that no faction has captured this and there are AI defenders. Enemy Faction Captured COPs, signified by a purple marker on the Map means that a different faction has cleared the AI and it is safe to be captured by your faction. Ally Faction Captured COPs, signified by a blue marker on the Map means that your faction has captured this COP and you can access its features. These are the outpost that can have Vulture vendor available. They are bigger than minor COPs, and also have more enemies when capturing them. Major Combat Outposts Stalwart 154:160 Westmore 168:161 Winchester 201:148 Harrison 197:125 Spielberk 182:123 Titan 153:121 Bronco 142:134 Crusader 137:151 Nomad 189:157 There are currently 27 Minor COPs. These smaller Combat Outposts aren't as heavily defended as their larger counterparts, but can still prove challenging. These COPs act in the same manner as the Major COPs but do not contain gear or weapon caches. They can't have Vulture available. Minor Combat Outposts Region Lancer 146:164 Atlas 141:158 Walker 137:163 Jefferson 174:115 Belfast 166:120 Wildcat 174:121 Vanguard 201:167 Tempest 204:158 Ripcord 197:162 Shepherd 192:150 Gator 204:142 Diamond 201:134 Eagle 177:126 Gladius 191:133 Warden 191:122 Arsenal 206:120 Bearcat 149:169 Panther 152:155 Thor 164:158 Argos 165:168 Blackjack 188:162 Tomahawk 177:163 Falcon 178:156 Mystic 133:154 Savanna 136:133 Aquila 135:142 Gladiator 165:128 Cobra 154:127 Knight 147:123 Landing Zones (LZs) are designated locations across the island where operators can call in a Little Bird helicopter for transport or use them as extraction points for exfiltration back to the Main Base. For landing zones to be accessible, the player must first discover them by walking within a ~100m radius of one. Players may request transportation between landing zones. When requesting transport to somewhere, the helicopter will pick up the player from the closest LZ to them. There are 15 total faction locked LZs, 5 around each Faction Base. These are inaccessible to members of other factions.

raw.name: Looting
raw.content: Looting is the main source for acquiring Loot, gear and weapons scattered throughout the map. The locker is a safe location for players to store their items. Depending on the edition of the game purchased, the locker will be a different size: 10x25 on Standard Edition 10x35 on Tactical Edition 10x45 on Elite Edition 10x60 on Supporter Edition The locker size can be upgraded via the DLC packs, found on the Steam Store , or by leveling your PMC up in game. 10x35 is unlocked at PMC Level 20 10x45 is unlocked at PMC Level 30 10x60 is unlocked at PMC Level 40 The equipment screen is where players can equip weapons and gear on their character. Before deploying to the battle field, you can place whatever you want to bring into battle. Once in battle, everything you brought in with you with the exception of the Secure Lockbox and their contents, as well as Melee weapons, can be lost. In your inventory, you can equip a primary weapon , Headwear , Glasses , Headsets , Armor Vests and Tactical Rigs . Additionally, you can equip gear in your Carriers section that will hold items such as a Plate Carrier , Backpacks and Belts . Items inside carriers marked with a lightning bolt symbol (such as medicine , throwables or Provisions ), are available for quick access. Secure Lockboxes are containers that you can bring into battle which, along with their contents, will not be lost upon death. Every player starts with a lockbox depending on the edition of the game purchased. 2x2 Storage for the Safelock Protected Ruck Case 3x2 Storage for the Snuck 908 Portable Lockbox 3x3 Storage for the TAS Secure Case The Vendors are who you go to purchase equipment from. Money will be taken and deposited into your Locker. Depending on your reputation with the vendor, items may become available for purchase. Vendors also offer Tasks that require you to complete certain objectives for rewards that may include Gear, Money, Experience and Reputation. These containers have a limited assortment of loot that spawns inside of them. They reset once every 30 minutes if no players interacted with it. raw.name: Trading
raw.content: Trading is a big part of the economy in Lamang . Vendors provide each PMC faction's player with purchasable gear using money as currency. Each vendor specializes in a particular category of goods, be they headsets , headwears , glasses , plate carriers , Armor Vests , rigs , tools, weapons , ammunition , weapon parts , night vision devices , attachments or medical supplies. Vendors can also buy gear and items that have been looted or found on other players.
